newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Flags of two Chinas raised over Japan-held isles.
newsitem.headline: Flags of two Chinas raised over Japan-held isles.

text.p: Activists raised the national flags of both communist China and Taiwan's exiled Republic of China in a brazen landing early on Monday on an East China Sea archipelago held by Japan, Taiwan Television reported.
"They have put up two flags on a hill on the island. One is the Republic of China flag. The other is the five-star flag" of the People's of Republic China, the state-run station said.
"Everyone aboard the boats offshore let up a great cheer when they saw the flags," a Taiwan state radio reporter told his station by ship-to-shore radio.

Reports from the flotilla of 50 protest boats said a force of up to 30 Japanese coastal patrol vessels sought to repulse the landing by positioning themselves between small landing craft and the islands claimed by Japan as the Senkakus and by Taiwan and China as the Diaoyus.
"It was very difficult to break through the Japanese ship cordon as the ships tried to collide with us, but we did it," the state radio reporter said.
The captain of one protest boat told Taiwan radio that his vessel had been butted by a Japanese patrol boat and sustained minor damage. No injuries were reported.
